about: Where Portland businesses can donate surplus food and supplies. Used by donate.html. Separate from resources.json, which is a shared contract read by other apps. Public domain (CC0). Verify every change before committing: see CONTRIBUTING.md.

recipients.name: Urban Gleaners
recipients.desc: Rescues extra food from restaurants, grocers, caterers and offices and gives it out at free food markets around Portland.
recipients.acceptsText: Fresh produce, unserved leftovers from catered events, and food past its "best by" date that is still good. Everything must be clean and unopened.
recipients.notAccepted: Opened packages or spoiled food. Ask yourself: would you eat it?
recipients.pickupText: Sometimes available for donations over 100 lbs, one-time or on a regular schedule. They can bring bins and insulated carriers (cambros).
recipients.leadTime: Call or email to set up a pickup. Leave a voicemail and they call back. Lead time not stated.
recipients.minimum: Over 100 lbs for a pickup. No minimum stated for drop-off.

recipients.name: Blanchet House
recipients.sub: Free meals, Old Town: food rescue and clothing
recipients.desc: Serves about 1,000 free meals a day, Mon-Sat. Takes large amounts of fresh, unexpired and soon-to-expire food from restaurants, grocers, wholesalers and bakeries.
recipients.acceptsText: Fruits, vegetables, meats, dry goods and spices, best in bulk: large amounts of one item. Unopened catered trays: call first to check. Clothing: new socks and men's underwear, coats, hats, gloves, adult sweats and jeans, blankets, sleeping bags.
recipients.notAccepted: Partly eaten or served food. Canned food drives unless arranged first. Children's clothes, dress clothes, linens, home goods.
recipients.pickupText: Restaurant, catering and other business pickups by arrangement. They don't pick up from homes.
recipients.dropoffText: Food: Mon-Sat, closed Sunday. Call before you come. Clothing: Mon-Sat 8-10:30am or 1:30-4pm.
recipients.leadTime: Call or email to arrange a pickup. Lead time not stated.

recipients.name: Oregon Food Bank
recipients.sub: Food industry donations: a few cases to full truckloads
recipients.desc: Takes extra food from growers, manufacturers, grocers and distributors and sends it to food pantries across Oregon and SW Washington.
recipients.acceptsText: Overages, short-dated products, mislabeled products (they can fix labels), and rejected or mis-shipped loads. Focus on produce, protein, dairy and pantry staples.
recipients.dropoffText: At their warehouses, by arrangement. Call or email first. They review each donation and plan the drop-off with you.
recipients.leadTime: Time-critical donations welcome. Call, email or use their form and they follow up.
recipients.minimum: None stated. "From full truckloads to a few cases."

recipients.name: Milk Crate Kitchen
recipients.sub: Cooks rescued food into family meals
recipients.desc: Chef-led nonprofit that cooks meals from scratch using rescued food. Works with farmers, food makers and other businesses.
recipients.acceptsText: "Certain" perishable and nonperishable items. They prefer whole foods in bulk sizes or packaging.
recipients.dropoffText: Email to arrange. No drop-off address or hours published.

recipients.name: Portland Rescue Mission
recipients.desc: Shelter and recovery programs. Lists fruit, vegetables, bottled water and coffee among its most-needed items, plus toiletries and clothing.
recipients.acceptsText: Fruit, vegetables, bottled water, coffee. Travel-size toiletries, razors, deodorant, women's hygiene products, hair products. New undergarments, socks, jeans, coats, hats, gloves, twin blankets, backpacks.
recipients.dropoffText: Burnside Shelter is open 24/7. The lobby may close for cleaning 6-6:45am and 5-5:45pm. Short-term street parking by the front door.
recipients.leadTime: Not stated. For prepared or refrigerated food, call first: their site doesn't say whether they take it.

recipients.name: William Temple House
recipients.desc: Food pantry and social services. Takes shelf-stable food and fresh produce.
recipients.acceptsText: Non-perishable food (canned vegetables, soup, meat, ready-to-eat meals, nut butters, cooking oil) and fresh produce.
recipients.notAccepted: Anything that needs a fridge or freezer, like meat and dairy.
recipients.dropoffText: Hoyt office during food pantry hours or by appointment. Or the donation barrel at their thrift store, 2230 NW Glisan St, Tue-Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 11am-6pm.
recipients.leadTime: Call to arrange a drop-off time.

recipients.name: Lift UP
recipients.desc: Food pantry and grocery delivery for low-income neighbors downtown and in Northwest Portland.
recipients.acceptsText: Food that is sealed and labeled.
recipients.dropoffText: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 10am-3pm. Call to confirm where to drop off: their site lists both the pantry and an office address.

recipients.name: SnowCap Community Charities
recipients.desc: Food pantry and basic needs for East Multnomah County.
recipients.acceptsText: Commercially packaged food (canned, boxed, fresh, frozen and dried), baby food and formula, pet food. New socks, blankets, personal care and hygiene products.

recipients.name: Portland Fruit Tree Project
recipients.sub: Northeast Fruit Fridge: small amounts of produce
recipients.desc: Outdoor community fridge for fresh produce. Best for a few boxes, not pallets.
recipients.acceptsText: All kinds of fresh produce, including vegetables and herbs. Sort it into A-grade (store quality) and B-grade (fine to eat now or preserve).
recipients.notAccepted: Fruit that fell on the ground (E. coli risk), or produce only good for compost.
recipients.dropoffText: Leaven Community Center parking lot, open 24/7. No need to call.

recipients.name: p:ear
recipients.desc: Youth drop-in center in Old Town. Takes winter gear, personal care items and food for its kitchen.
recipients.acceptsText: Non-perishable food (high quality, organic), rice and pasta. Through Jan 31, 2027: new adult socks and underwear, waterproof outerwear, sleeping bags, tarps, travel-size toiletries, razors, body wipes. Groups can also sign up to bring pre-cooked meals ("meal train").
recipients.dropoffText: By appointment only. Call or email to schedule.

recipients.name: Transition Projects
recipients.desc: Runs shelters and housing programs. Takes new hygiene items and adult clothing at its donation desk.
recipients.acceptsText: Hygiene items must be new and unopened. Clothing must be clean, laundered, in season, and free of stains, holes and pet hair. Most needed: men's and women's underwear, towels, men's pants.
recipients.notAccepted: Children's items, camping gear, household items, sports equipment, formal wear, medical equipment.
recipients.dropoffText: Tue 9am-noon, Wed 3-6pm, Fri 9am-noon. No drop-offs outside these times without an appointment (email volunteer@tprojects.org).

recipients.name: Rose Haven
recipients.sub: Day center for women, children and gender-diverse people
recipients.desc: Day shelter in Northwest Portland. Always needs full-size hygiene items, blankets and new underwear.
recipients.acceptsText: Full-size hygiene items, new underwear, in-season clothing, blankets, sleeping bags, tents and tarps.
recipients.notAccepted: Opened or used hygiene products and make-up, used socks and underwear, clothing with holes, stains or pet hair, medication.
recipients.dropoffText: Tuesdays 1-3pm. Pull up at the loading dock on Glisan and ring the bell at the metal donation door. Other times by appointment only.

recipients.name: JOIN
recipients.desc: Helps people move from the street into housing. Takes adult clothing, hygiene products and survival gear.
recipients.acceptsText: New and used adult clothing in all seasons (clean and freshly washed), sturdy shoes and boots, hats and gloves. Hygiene products: travel-size is best, full-size is fine.
recipients.dropoffText: Mon-Fri 11am-2pm at the Day Space. Call ahead so someone can help: 971-284-2173.

law.title: Federal: Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act
text: A business that donates food in good faith to a nonprofit, for people in need at no cost (or at a price that only covers handling and transport), is not civilly or criminally liable for the food's nature, age, packaging or condition. The food has to meet quality and labeling standards. It can be surplus, short-dated or not pretty enough to sell.

Since January 2023, grocers, wholesalers, farms, food processors and distributors, restaurants, caterers, schools and colleges are also protected when they give food directly to a person in need at no cost.
It doesn't protect gross negligence or intentional misconduct, and it doesn't replace state or local health rules.

law.title: Oregon: ORS 30.890 (food)
text: A good-faith donor of food that looks fit to eat, given to a charity or nonprofit (including a food bank) to hand out free or on a sliding scale, is not subject to criminal penalty or civil damages from the food's condition. Restaurants and other licensed food businesses are named as donors. Meat, dairy, eggs, bakery, produce, and refrigerated or frozen food are all covered.
It doesn't protect gross negligence, recklessness or intentional conduct.

law.title: Oregon: ORS 30.892 (supplies and clothing)
text: Stores, wholesalers and manufacturers that donate usable merchandise in good faith to a charity or nonprofit get the same protection. That includes toiletries, clothing and household items. The protection ends if the item is resold.
